header.running_head: The Sahabah (RA) Exercise Patience on the Occasions of Death

blocks.text: were then taken away while that of Hadhrat Hamzah (RA) was left. Thereafter, another nine bodies were brought and Rasulullaah ﷺ performed the Janaazah salaah for them with seven Takbeers. These bodies were then carried away while that of Hadhrat Hamzah (RA) was left behind. Yet again, another nine bodies were brought and Rasulullaah ﷺ performed the Janaazah salaah for them also with seven Takbeers. These bodies were then carried away while that of Hadhrat Hamzah (RA) was left behind. This continued until Rasulullaah ﷺ had performed the Janaazah salaah for them all.[^1]

Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awaam (RA) narrates, "A woman came running during the Battle of Uhud and would have seen the dead bodies when Rasulullaah ﷺ called out, '(Stop) The woman! (Stop) The woman!' Rasulullaah ﷺ disliked that women should see the bodies. When I guessed that she was my mother Safiyya (RA), I ran to her and reached her before she could reach the dead. She was a strong woman and struck me in the chest saying, 'Get away from me. The ground does not belong to you!' I said, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ has emphatically prohibited you form going there.' She then halted in her tracks and took out two sheets saying, 'I have brought these two sheets for my brother Hamzah. The news of his death has already reached me and I want you to bury him in these.'
We then took the sheets to enshroud Hamzah (RA) in but found next to him someone from the Ansaar who was also killed and mutilated as Hamzah (RA) was. Because we felt difficult to enshroud Hamzah (RA) in two sheets while the Ansaari had none, we decided that one sheet would be used for Hamzah (RA) and the other for the Ansaari. After measuring the two sheets, we found the one to be larger than the other. (To decide who would have which sheet) We then drew lots between the two and enshrouded each one in the sheet that fell to his lot."[^2]

Discussing the martyrdom of Hadhrat Hamzah (RA), it is reported that when Hadhrat Safiyyah bint Abdul Muttalib (RA) came to see her brother, Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) met her saying, "Dear mother! It is the instruction of Rasulullaah ﷺ that you return." She said, "Why should I? I have already heard that my brother's body has been mutilated. This has taken place for the sake of Allaah and we are pleased with it (with Allaah's decree). I shall definitely exercise patience and look forward to the rewards from Allaah." When Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) reported her words to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Let her go." She then went to the body of Hadhrat Hamzah (RA) and prayed for his forgiveness. Rasulullaah ﷺ then gave instructions for him to be buried.[^3]

Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.197). Ibn Abi Shaybah and Tabraani have reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA), as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.170). Bazzaar has also reported a similar narration, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.6 Pg.118).
Bazzaar, Ahmad and Abu Ya'la. Haythami (Vol.6 Pg.118) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Ibn Is'haaq, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.4 Pg.349).
